historical_record.description: The building had been occupied by two dwelling units since at least 1943.
The building was legalized as a two-family dwelling in an R-1 district in 1965.
The City Planning Commission unanimously disapproved a building permit to expand the two-unit building, recommending that the substandard second unit be removed if the main unit were enlarged.
A building permit for alterations, approved by the neighbours, was issued for the property in 1971.
A two-unit building, a legal non-conforming use with a substandard second dwelling unit, occupied the property.
The building was a legal non-conforming two-family dwelling in an R-1 district; excavation beneath it had reached more than 9 feet without the required engineering approval.

The City Planning Commission unanimously continued its discretionary review of alterations to the two-family dwelling to September 13, 1973, directing that all construction stop meanwhile except work needed for the safety of the adjoining building.

The dwelling on the north side of the 300 block of Cumberland Street had two floors of living space totalling about 1,470 square feet as a two-family dwelling, no off-street parking, and was under a long-standing Building Inspection condemnation order.

The City Planning Commission unanimously resolved that the building permit to alter the two-family dwelling be disapproved unless the basement ceiling was kept to 7 feet, the basement stayed within the existing walls, and a recorded restriction barred living use of the basement.
